/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 15 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3151 (-44)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5173 (-143)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2521 (18)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1565 (7)
Baltic Handysize Index: 850 (-1)
CAPESIZE
Following holidays across several countries yesterday, the week concluded on a notably subdued note, with activity across both basins lacking conviction and trading volumes thinning into the close. The BCI 182 5TC fell by $1,293 to settle at $46,916, reflecting the softer overall tone despite underlying support remaining in both basins. In the Pacific, conditions were generally steady but uninspiring, with limited fresh enquiry and reduced miner participation weighing on sentiment. Two C5 miners were initially reported in the market, although trading activity remained extremely thin throughout the session. C5 declined by 0.423 to $15.010, with market talk suggesting an overage vessel fixed at $14.90, and low $15s had been paid otherwise little concluded business emerged before the close. The Atlantic remained comparatively firmer structurally, particularly in the North Atlantic where tonnage continues to appear tight. South Brazil and West Africa to China business also retained underlying support, although activity levels were similarly limited. On C3, a widening gap developed for index dates, with bids reportedly around $36.50 against offers closer to $37.50, restricting liquidity. Nevertheless, $36.75 was again heard fixed for early June and 10/15 June laycans, helping keep the route relatively stable overall, with C3 easing marginally by $0.125 to $36.800.
PANAMAX
A quieter end to the week was observed compared to the flurry of activity seen earlier, with the P5TC improving by $163 to $22,691. The trans Atlantic market is said by brokers to be maintaining its positive sentiment, with higher levels continuing to be discussed. The North Atlantic has also been highlighted by some as looking slim in relation to the volume of offers being discussed. Fronthaul activity moved sideways today with brokers noting that following the European holidays and with it being Friday many market participants have stepped back to reassess conditions. In the Pacific, sentiment remains mixed. Some suggest that increasing tonnage supply may begin to outweigh cargo demand, while others maintain that activity across Indonesia, Australia, and the North Pacific remains healthy, supporting a positive outlook. Offers are generally being held at previous levels, creating a sense of stand-off in the market. Period activity has been active, with the ETG Aquarius (81,976 2022) open North China 1/10 June reportedly placed on subjects for short period with Mingwah. Meanwhile the Zhong Chang Zhou Shan (75,409 2013) open Gunsan 27/30 May, is also said to be on subjects for 5–7 months at $19,300, with the charterer undisclosed.

Atlantic
The Agios Georgios S (75,041 2012) open in Kandla 16/17 May has now been linked to Messrs Bunge for a trip via East Coast South America to Singapore-Japan at $19,500. Koch have been linked with the Risoluto (82,718 2025) open Gibraltar 23/25 May for a trip to the Far East with grains at $35,000.

Asia
The Adriatica Graeca II (82,000 2026) open in Zhoushan 16/17 May was discussed as being place on subjects but no further details have emerged.
SUPRAMAX
A typical slow end to the week after yesterday’s Ascension Day holiday, with many players in the Atlantic staying away from their desks. The South American market remained relatively firm with a good supply of fresh cargo brokers said, although fresh fixing information remained lacking. The US Gulf was balanced, whilst the Continent-Mediterranean lacked fresh impetus. The Asian arena saw mixed fortunes from an owners' perspective whilst the north remained in positive territory, brokers said the fresh enquiry was slowing further south which in turn was putting downward pressure on rates. The 11TC average did however remain in positive motion gaining a further $90 to finish at $19,788.

Atlantic
The Aquarius (56,048 2013) open EC Mexico fixed for a trip with grains basis delivery SW Pass trip West Mediterranean at $20,000 to Bunge. The HSL Mexico (61,167 2020) open Altamira fixed for a trip with grains again delivery SW Pass to Japan at $25,000 with MOL. Also, the Jade Wealth (64,301 2024) open Mississippi River fixed for trip with grains to EC Mexico at $19,000 to Ultrabulk.

Asia
Little fresh activity surfaced, but from the Indian Ocean the Allis Serene (58,098 2011) was heard fixed Goa 18/20 May trip via New Mangalore redelivery Mombasa at $18,000 to Team Bulk.

HANDYSIZE
It was a typical quiet Friday for the Handy sector, with minimal visible activity. The Baltic Handysize Index remained at 850 while the 7TC average down by $15, closed at $15,296. In the Continent and Mediterranean, market fundamentals and rate levels stayed largely unchanged. In the South Atlantic, the outlook continue to remain soft due a lengthy tonnage list and limited demand. Meanwhile, the U.S. Gulf appeared rather subdued, with no change in its fundamentals. In the Pacific, the market saw a slower day with owners were willing to wait as rates were trending upwards. Charterers with prompt cargoes were actively looking to cover them, however rates are being recorded around the last done levels.

Market Fundamentals
CISA Daily Crude Steel Production

After declining in late-April, daily crude steel production at Chinese Iron and Steel Association (CISA) member mills rose 3.6% from the preceding ten days to 2.1 Mt/day in the period 1-10 May, according to the industry association. However, output stood 4.3% below the same period last year. As of 10 May, finished steel inventories of large and medium-sized enterprises in China also rose, up 9.4% from end-April to 16.9 Mt. The rise in stocks was faster than the lift in daily crude steel output since the Labour Day holiday (1-5 May) resulted in slack demand from downstream users. In the week to 8 May, the percentage of profitable Blast Furnace steel mills climbed 9.1 percentage points from the prior week to 60.2%, the highest since September 2025, MySteel data show.

Meanwhile, Chinese iron ore imports lifted 0.7 Mt year-on-year to 103.8 Mt in April, despite lower shipments from Australia and heavy rain in Brazil.

ALSO CONTINUED TO POST GAINS ALONGSIDE THE BROADER PACIFIC RALLY. HOWEVER, BY MIDWEEK ONWARDS, MOMENTUM BEGAN TO FADE AS CARGO ENQUIRY SLOWED NOTICEABLY ACROSS MOST REGIONS AND CHARTERERS STARTED PULLING BACK AFTER THE SHARP RUN UP IN RATES. FFAS ALSO TURNED SOFTER ACROSS THE CURVE DURING THE LATTER PART OF THE WEEK, REFLECTING GROWING CAUTION AROUND WHETHER THE MARKET COULD SUSTAIN SUCH ELEVATED LEVELS. ALTHOUGH INDICES REMAINED POSITIVE, DESPITE THE SOFTER SENTIMENT SEEN TOWARDS THE END OF THE WEEK, THE MARKET CONTINUED TO HOLD RELATIVELY FIRM OVERALL, WITH RATES MANAGING TO MAINTAIN MOST OF THE GAINS ACHIEVED EARLIER IN THE WEEK. TO ACHIEVE AROUND THE $24,000 LEVELS. HOWEVER, AS THE WEEK PROGRESSED, ENQUIRY BEGAN MOVING FURTHER FORWARD INTO MID-JUNE DATES AND THE AMOUNT OF FRESH CIRCULATION SLOWED. WHILE TONNAGE IN THE NORTH REDUCED TOWARDS THE END OF THE WEEK, THE SLOWER PACE OF FRESH DEMAND AND INCREASINGLY CAUTIOUS CHARTERER SENTIMENT RESULTED IN THE MARKET LOSING SOME MOMENTUM AFTER ITS STRONG START. AUSTRALIA WAS UNDOUBTEDLY THE STRONGEST PERFORMING REGION, WITH AGGRESSIVE FIXING ACTIVITY AND TIGHT PROMPT DEMAND DRIVING RATES SHARPLY HIGHER. EAUS ROUNDS ACHIEVED PREMIUM LEVELS, SUPPORTED BY STRONG EARLY JUNE DEMAND AND LIMITED PROMPT SUPPLY. HOWEVER, THE MARKET COOLED NOTICEABLY FROM MIDWEEK ONWARDS AS THE STRONG SECOND HALF MAY MOMENTUM FAILED TO PROPERLY ROLL INTO JUNE. FRESH CARGO ENQUIRY BECAME INCREASINGLY THIN, WITH ACTIVITY MAINLY LIMITED TO A HANDFUL OF CHINA STEMS FOR EARLY JUNE LAYCANS. DESPITE RATES REMAINING ELEVATED, SENTIMENT SOFTENED CONSIDERABLY AS CHARTERERS STEPPED BACK AND ADOPTED A MORE CAUTIOUS WAIT-AND-SEE APPROACH AFTER THE RAPID RISE SEEN EARLIER IN THE WEEK. INDO SAW SOME IMPROVEMENT AT THE START OF THE WEEK COMPARED TO PREVIOUS WEEKS, PARTICULARLY FOR LATER MAY DATES. HOWEVER, THE MARKET GRADUALLY LOST MOMENTUM THROUGH THE SECOND HALF OF THE WEEK AS INDONESIAN COAL ENQUIRY SLOWED SIGNIFICANTLY, ESPECIALLY INTO SOUTHEAST ASIA. CHINESE COAL TRADING ALSO BECAME QUIETER AMID VOLATILITY IN THE UNDERLYING COMMODITY MARKET, FURTHER WEIGHING ON SENTIMENT. BY FRIDAY, INDO DEMAND SEEMED THIN OVERALL, WITH FRESH CARGO COUNT REMAINING WELL BELOW LEVELS SEEN IN RECENT WEEKS. OVERALL, WHILE THE PACIFIC MARKET MANAGED TO HOLD ONTO MOST OF THE GAINS ACHIEVED EARLIER IN THE WEEK, THE BASIN CLEARLY LOST STEAM DURING THE LATTER HALF AS CARGO ENQUIRY SLOWED AND CHARTERERS RESISTED HIGHER LEVELS. UNDERLYING COAL FUNDAMENTALS REMAIN SUPPORTIVE, BUT WITH QUIETER CARGO VOLUMES, FLATTER FFAS AND INCREASINGLY CAUTIOUS SENTIMENT, THE MARKET LOOKS SET TO ENTER NEXT WEEK ON A MORE STABLE AND QUIETER FOOTING RATHER THAN CONTINUING THE SHARP UPWARD TRAJECTORY SEEN AT THE START OF THIS WEEK. THAT SAID, EVEN WITH SOFTER SENTIMENT DEVELOPING TOWARDS THE END OF THE WEEK, THE MARKET HAS STILL MANAGED TO HOLD ONTO ITS ELEVATED LEVELS RELATIVELY WELL, SUGGESTING UNDERLYING SUPPORT REMAINS FIRMLY IN PLACE FOR NOW.
